clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old male presented with a long-standing, painless, gradually growing right facial swelling since childhood. Clinical examination revealed a fluctuant, compressible, soft swelling with slight rise in surface temperature, jaw deviation, and intraoral bluish-red discoloration with pulsation. Conventional panoramic and submentovertex radiographs showed multiple concentric calcifications suggestive of phleboliths. Based on these typical clinical and radiographic findings, a diagnosis of hemangioma of the face was made. The patient was subsequently referred to interventional radiology for management, but the outcome of this referral is not documented.
